evals.prompt: Write a production Dockerfile for a Node.js 22 web service that builds TypeScript with `npm run build` and serves on port 3000. Keep the final image as small and secure as reasonably possible.
assertions: Uses a multi-stage build with at least one named build stage (`AS <name>`) and a separate final runtime stage that only pulls in built artifacts via `COPY --from=<stage>`

The final runtime stage uses a minimal base image (distroless such as `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22`, or a slim/alpine variant) rather than a full node image, and does NOT reinstall build/dev dependencies
The container runs as a non-root user (a `USER` line such as `USER nonroot` / `USER node` or an explicitly created non-root user)

evals.prompt: Our Docker builds re-run `npm ci` on almost every commit even when only application source changed, and installing system packages with apt-get bloats the image. Show the Dockerfile layer ordering and the apt-get command you would use to fix both problems.
assertions: Copies the lockfile/manifest (e.g. `package-lock.json` / `package.json`) and runs the dependency install BEFORE copying the rest of the source (`COPY . .` comes after the install step)
Combines `apt-get update`, `apt-get install`, and `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` into a single `RUN` instruction (chained with `&&`) so the apt cache is not left in an earlier layer

evals.prompt: Add a database password to a containerized Node app without baking the secret into the image, and make sure the build context does not leak local files. Provide the relevant Dockerfile/compose lines and any supporting file.
assertions: The secret is passed at runtime via a file-based mechanism (e.g. a `*_FILE` env var pointing at `/run/secrets/...`, a Compose `secrets:` section, or a BuildKit `--mount=type=secret`) and is NOT `COPY`/`ADD`ed into the image or hardcoded in a plain `ENV`/`environment` value
Includes a `.dockerignore` that excludes at least `node_modules/` and `.git/` (or `.git`)

evals.prompt: Add a container health check to a Node.js image so a Kubernetes/Compose orchestrator can detect when the app stops responding. Show the Dockerfile instruction.
assertions: Uses the `HEALTHCHECK` instruction with tuning flags such as `--interval`, `--timeout`, and/or `--start-period`, and a `CMD` that exits non-zero on failure (e.g. `|| exit 1`)
